blockers.summary: Market analytics and event analytics share the analytics name but expose incompatible routes and runtime requirements.
blockers.resolution: Give each domain an unambiguous service name, URL, ownership map and gateway prefix; prove every deployed route reaches the intended binary.

blockers.summary: Legacy public, authenticated and admin market-analytics paths/envelopes do not have a proven compatibility layer.
blockers.resolution: Lock method, path, query, status and response adapters for every source surface and fail unknown drift closed.

blockers.summary: The standalone market service has hermetic direct-JWT, wallet-propagation, and authenticated authority-failure boundaries, and authority errors stop before provider work; A2.10 adds an exported but unwired server-side workload-auth composition, while analytics metadata, a concrete credential verifier, TLS, owner delegation, authoritative entitlement success, live runtime and production ownership remain unproven.
blockers.resolution: Retain strict service verification, canonical-wallet derivation, fail-closed authority errors and A2.10 ordering while proving compatibility, analytics credential injection, trusted workload verification, owner delegation, TLS, authoritative entitlement success, runtime, routing and cutover behavior.

blockers.summary: A2.5 hermetically bounds canonical request size, process-local concurrency, transient attempts, deadline and outward failure details; provenance, licensing, normalization, distributed quotas, freshness and cache semantics remain unproven.

blockers.summary: Analytics, authenticated portfolio, and the home market preview now fail closed without verified market/owner loaders; none has production-complete market UX.

blockers.summary: Search, filters, sorting, pagination, export and watchlist interactions are not proven against live backend state.

blockers.summary: A2.6 removes the market client's silent authenticated free-plan fallback, A2.7 proves the pure resolver, A2.8 adds a static core-owned snapshot adapter, A2.9 removes the unsafe identity event listener, A2.10 adds an exported fail-closed authenticated RPC composition, and A2.11 extracts the adapter behind a library-only package boundary; identity requests fail closed because the composition and store are unwired, SQL is unexecuted against a certified schema, and concrete credential trust, analytics metadata, TLS, owner delegation, reconciliation and runtime activation are absent.
blockers.resolution: Keep the pure resolver, fail-closed market boundary, extracted static store and A2.10 auth-before-wallet/query ordering; certify credential trust and rotation, inject analytics metadata, define owner delegation and TLS, certify the adopted schema and query plan, reconcile source lifecycle and alternate entitlement semantics, then prove free, paid, expiry, overlap, downgrade, outage and recovery parity before runtime activation.

blockers.summary: A2.9 removes the public identity emit and stream mounts, but no authenticated authoritative publisher identity, exact audience or replay protection exists for a durable replacement.

ownershipRules.rule: Market analytics owns market-provider normalization and ranking query execution, not plan decisions.
Event analytics owns append-only product events and derived aggregates, not financial truth.
Indexer owns canonical chain projections and never fabricates or authoritatively changes payment state.
Identity owns the wallet-to-active-plan ranking-offset projection; frontend and market services do not compute it.
Authenticated owner keys come from verified canonical subjects, never request bodies, paths or forwarding headers.
Admin reads require admin audience plus exact read permission; mutations/internal operations require their exact manage identity.
Cross-domain joins are read models with provenance and revision metadata, never hidden shared-table ownership.

freshnessRules.rule: Every market response carries provider, observed-at, cache age and stale state.
A market-provider outage cannot turn fixtures or old cache data into an unlabeled live response.
Event aggregates expose an as-of watermark and late-event policy.
Indexer responses expose canonical/finalized status and indexed-head lag per chain.
Ranking-offset responses carry an entitlement projection revision and effective interval.
UI live/stale/offline labels are computed from backend freshness metadata.

backfillReconciliationRules.rule: Indexer backfills are bounded, leased, resumable, observable and idempotent per chain/range.
Reorg repair orphans and rebuilds all dependent transaction/log projections atomically.
Event migration backfills preserve source IDs and deduplicate repeated runs.
Revenue aggregates reconcile to finalized payment/subscription authority by period and currency.
Ranking offsets reconcile active plan assignments to the identity projection with repairable mismatches.
Market shadow results compare normalized filter/pagination/ranking outputs without writing source systems.
Every reconciliation emits counts, checksums, mismatch samples and a reviewed repair outcome.

observabilityRules.rule: Dependency-aware readiness distinguishes process liveness from usable service readiness.
Market metrics cover upstream latency/errors/throttling, cache age/hits and stale responses.
Event metrics cover accepted/rejected/deduplicated events, aggregation watermark and schema violations.
Indexer metrics cover canonical/finalized heads, lag, reorg depth, RPC errors and backfill progress.
Identity projection metrics cover query latency, authority failures, stream gaps and reconciliation mismatches.
Metrics endpoints are internal-only and alerts have owners, thresholds and runbooks.

cutoverRules.rule: Cut over one domain at a time behind an explicit route owner.
Shadow traffic is read-only or idempotently isolated and never creates dual write authority.
Promotion requires a recorded parity window, error budget and zero unresolved reconciliation drift.
Rollback restores the prior route owner without discarding newly accepted durable facts.
Production deployment remains a separate explicitly authorized action after readiness passes.

Frontend ranking loading is deliberately absent, while event tracking still swallows upstream failure.
Production manifests do not prove separately deployed event analytics and indexer workloads.
